scope: MiniMax-H3 static-reference test-time scaling for ordered T-shirt folding
summary: The frozen 10-candidate MiniMax-H3 test-time-scaling run completed at 24, 32, and 40 inference steps. All 10 proposals were rejected by the predeclared fail-closed gates: every candidate violated both sleeve-length invariants and the required fold/move ordering. No candidate is promoted or delivered. A continuous rigid-sleeve carrier was therefore added as a new architecture experiment rather than increasing seeds or relaxing thresholds.
evidence: All 10 candidate evidence files reject viewer_left_sleeve_length_conserved and viewer_right_sleeve_length_conserved
The frozen maximum sleeve-length relative-deviation threshold remained 0.08 for every candidate
The v2 carrier analytically preserves every declared sleeve material segment to floating-point tolerance across all 124 frames
lessons: Static scene identity plus a detailed causal language plan is insufficient to make H3 preserve sleeve material topology in this scene.
Test-time scaling diagnoses a systematic conditioning failure when all seeds and step budgets fail the same hard gates; further seed expansion is not evidence of progress.
A camera-frame carrier can encode ordered continuous motion while rigid sleeve transforms make declared material-segment conservation exact in the control signal.
limitations: The carrier's exact conservation is in the named 2-D camera-pixel frame and is not metric 3-D cloth, force, contact, collision, or real-robot evidence.
The carrier is a proposal-control signal and fails the generic optical-flow output evaluator under occlusion; it is not an accepted final video.
A carrier-conditioned H3 output has not yet passed every frozen output hard gate or native-resolution human review.
next_actions: Run the predeclared four-candidate carrier-conditioned H3 policy at 32 and 40 inference steps.
Evaluate each H3 output with the unchanged tracking contract and deliver only an all-gates-pass candidate.
